[[Category:Quantum physics]]
== 1. State wavefunctions describe everything ==

All '''accessible information''' about '''any physically-possible state of a quantum system''' is described by its '''state wavefunction''' 

$$
\psi(\vec r,t)
$$
where $\vec r=(x_1, y_1, z_1, x_2, y_2, z_2,\dots, x_n, y_n, z_n)$ contains spatial coordinates of all particles in the system.

<ref>{{#cite:Q3391}}</ref>

== 2. The square of state wavefunctions is the spatial probability density ==

The probability of finding a quantum system of one or multiple particles in a state where particle $1,2,\dots,i$ are located in volume elements $dx_1dy_1dz_1,\, dx_2,dy_2,dz_2,\dots,dx_i,dy_i,dz_i$

$$
P=\int \Psi ^* (r, t) \psi (r , t) d \tau
$$
where $dτ = dx_1dy_1dz_1\dots dx_ndy_ndz_n$

and

$$
\int \limits _{all space} \Psi ^* (r, t) \psi (r , t) d \tau = 1
$$
(since $\int \limits_{all space} P d\tau=1$)

<ref>{{#cite:Q3391}}</ref>

== 3. Every observable can be obtained from the state wavefunction with a dedicated [[operator]] ==

=== In arbitrary spatial dimension $\vec x$ ===

$$
\begin{cases}
\text{Momentum operator}: \hat {P} _x = -i \hbar \dfrac {\partial}{\partial x} \\
\text{Kinetic energy operator}: \hat {T} _x = \left ( -\dfrac {\hbar ^2}{2m} \right ) \dfrac {\partial ^2}{\partial x^2} 
\end{cases}
$$

<ref>{{#cite:Q3391}}</ref>

=== Aggregation over 3 dimensional space ===

$$
\begin{cases}
\text{Momentum operator}: \hat {p} = -i \hbar \nabla \\
\text{Kinetic energy operator}: \hat {T} = \left ( -\dfrac {\hbar ^2}{2m} \right ) \nabla ^2 
\end{cases}
$$

where $\nabla^2$ is the [[Laplacian]].

<ref>{{#cite:Q3391}}</ref>

== 4. The time-dependent Schrödinger equation governs the time development of state wavefunctions ==

$$
\hat{H}_Q (\vec r , t) \Psi (\vec r , t) = i \hbar \dfrac {\partial}{\partial t} \Psi (\vec r , t ) 
$$
where $\hat H_Q$ is the [[quantum Hamiltonian]].

<ref>{{#cite:Q3391}}</ref>

=== Special case: when $\hat H_Q$ is time-independent ===

then

$$
\Psi(\vec r,t)=e^{-i\nu t}\Psi(\vec r)
$$
where $\nu= \frac{E}{h}$

<ref>{{#cite:Q3391}}</ref>

== 5. Expected value of observables ==

Let $A$ be an observable corresponding to quantum [[operator]] $\hat A$, and $\langle A \rangle$ denotes its average value, then

in [[Dirac notation]]:

$$
\langle A\rangle(t)
=
\frac{\langle \psi(t)|\hat A|\psi(t)\rangle}{\langle \psi(t)|\psi(t)\rangle},
$$

Equivalently,

$$
\langle A\rangle(t)
=
\frac{
\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}
\overline \Psi(\vec r,t)\,
\bigl(\hat A_{\vec r}\Psi\bigr)(\vec r,t)\,
d \tau
}{
\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}
\overline \Psi(\vec r,t)\,
\Psi(\vec r,t)\,
d \tau
},
$$
where $dτ = dx_1dy_1dz_1\dots dx_ndy_ndz_n$.

<ref>{{#cite:Q3391}}</ref>

== 6. State wavefunction as an [[eigenfunction]] ==

If

$$
\hat {A} \Psi = a \Psi ,
$$

then the observable associated with $\hat A$ will always have value $a$.

<ref>{{#cite:Q3391}}</ref>
